notes: Plan changes: in 2.2, replaced s3-one-zone-ia-zone-loss with aws-backup-cross-account-copy to avoid a name giveaway and broaden backup coverage; replaced ec2-auto-scaling-elb-health-check-opt-in with ec2-auto-scaling-availability-zone-replacement to test failure recovery rather than a configuration default. In 3.1, replaced efs-concurrent-nfs-clients with fsx-windows-self-managed-active-directory to broaden workload compatibility coverage and avoid overlap. In 3.2, replaced ec2-enhanced-networking-sriov with ec2-efa-os-bypass-communication to test communication behavior rather than implementation terminology. The Aurora scaling card retains its planned factKey and uses the current documentation name, Amazon Aurora serverless.

cards.statement: An Amazon RDS Multi-AZ DB instance deployment can serve read queries from its standby.
cards.explanation: The standby in an RDS Multi-AZ DB instance deployment is reserved for failover and does not serve application reads.
cards.misconception: A Multi-AZ DB instance standby also provides read-scaling capacity.

source.title: Multi-AZ DB instance deployments for Amazon RDS

cards.statement: Amazon Aurora's tier-based failover ranking places replica size ahead of configured promotion priority.
cards.explanation: Aurora's tier-based selection favors the highest-priority eligible replica. Instance size breaks ties between replicas with the same priority.
cards.misconception: Aurora ranks replica size ahead of configured promotion priority.

source.title: High availability for Amazon Aurora

cards.statement: Cached DNS answers can delay client switchover during Amazon Route 53 failover.
cards.explanation: DNS resolvers can retain an earlier Route 53 answer until its time to live expires. Failover routing changes do not immediately replace those cached answers.

source.title: Best practices for Amazon Route 53 DNS

cards.statement: A subnet-based NAT gateway can maintain egress for other zones during an outage of its own Availability Zone.
cards.explanation: A subnet-based NAT gateway is redundant within its Availability Zone. If that zone fails, other zones relying on that gateway lose their egress path.
cards.misconception: A subnet-based NAT gateway's managed redundancy extends across Availability Zones.

source.title: NAT gateway basics

cards.statement: AWS Backup supports copying backups into another AWS account within the same AWS Organizations organization.
cards.explanation: For supported resources, AWS Backup can place a backup copy in another account's vault. The separate copy remains available if the original backup is accidentally deleted.

source.title: Creating backup copies across AWS accounts

cards.statement: An Amazon EFS Regional file system supports mount targets in multiple Availability Zones.
cards.explanation: An EFS Regional file system can expose a mount target in each Availability Zone of its VPC, providing separate zonal network access points to the same file system.

source.title: Managing mount targets

cards.statement: A pilot light recovery environment keeps a scaled-down, fully functional application ready to serve traffic.
cards.explanation: Pilot light keeps core services running but requires application resources to be started or deployed during recovery. Warm standby keeps a scaled-down, functional application running.
cards.misconception: Pilot light has the same immediately functional application footprint as warm standby.

source.title: Disaster recovery options in the cloud

cards.statement: A recovery point objective defines the acceptable time needed to restore service after a disaster.
cards.explanation: A recovery point objective specifies acceptable data loss expressed as time. A recovery time objective specifies acceptable service-restoration delay.
cards.misconception: The recovery point objective measures restoration downtime rather than potential data loss.

source.title: REL13-BP01 Define recovery objectives for downtime and data loss

cards.statement: A disaster recovery Region can need higher service quotas before a standby scales to production capacity.
cards.explanation: Recovery Region quotas need to accommodate the workload after failover. Quotas sufficient for a small standby can still prevent it from expanding to production size.

source.title: Disaster recovery options in the cloud

cards.statement: Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling can replace capacity in other configured zones when an Availability Zone becomes unavailable.
cards.explanation: A multi-zone Auto Scaling group can launch replacement instances in its healthy configured zones, subject to available capacity, when launches fail in an impaired zone.

source.title: Auto Scaling benefits for application architecture

cards.statement: AWS CloudFormation supports returning a stack to its pre-update configuration after an update fails.
cards.explanation: CloudFormation rollback attempts to return resources to their pre-update configuration. A resource that cannot be restored can interrupt rollback and require intervention.

source.title: Continue rolling back an update

cards.statement: Amazon RDS Proxy drops idle application connections when switching to a replacement writer during failover.
cards.explanation: RDS Proxy preserves idle client connections while reconnecting to the replacement writer. Statements or transactions in progress can still fail.
cards.misconception: Database failover through RDS Proxy requires idle clients to establish new connections.

source.title: RDS Proxy concepts and terminology

cards.statement: An Amazon EBS volume can attach directly to an Amazon EC2 instance in another Availability Zone.
cards.explanation: An EBS volume and the EC2 instance using it must be in the same Availability Zone. Direct volume attachment does not cross that zonal boundary.
cards.misconception: EBS volumes support direct attachment to instances across Availability Zones.

source.title: Amazon EBS volumes

cards.statement: Amazon EBS gp3 volumes support simultaneous attachment to several EC2 instances in the same Availability Zone.
cards.explanation: EBS Multi-Attach supports Provisioned IOPS SSD io1 and io2 volumes, rather than gp3 volumes. Choosing gp3 rules out that shared-block-device configuration.
cards.misconception: The gp3 volume type supports EBS Multi-Attach.
cards.volatilityNote: The volume types eligible for EBS Multi-Attach could expand.

source.title: Attach an EBS volume to multiple EC2 instances using Multi-Attach

cards.statement: Amazon EBS gp3 permits IOPS increases independently of storage-capacity increases.
cards.explanation: With gp3, provisioned performance can be increased separately from storage size, within the volume's supported performance limits.

source.title: Amazon EBS General Purpose SSD volumes

cards.statement: Amazon EBS st1 volumes are tuned for frequent small, random database operations.
cards.explanation: The st1 volume type is designed for large, sequential I/O such as log processing. Small, random database operations are a poor match for this HDD access pattern.
cards.misconception: Throughput-oriented HDD storage suits small, random database I/O.

source.title: Amazon EBS Throughput Optimized HDD and Cold HDD volumes

cards.statement: Amazon EC2 instance store can preserve its data through a stop-and-start cycle of the instance.
cards.explanation: Stopping an EC2 instance discards its instance store data. Data that needs to survive a stop-and-start cycle requires persistent storage elsewhere.
cards.misconception: Instance store data survives an instance stop as long as the instance is later restarted.

source.title: Data persistence for Amazon EC2 instance store volumes

cards.statement: Amazon FSx for Windows File Server can join an existing self-managed Microsoft Active Directory domain.
cards.explanation: An FSx for Windows File Server file system can join a self-managed domain during creation. This supports integration with existing directory identities and resources.
tags: Amazon FSx for Windows File Server

source.title: Using a self-managed Microsoft Active Directory

cards.statement: An Amazon FSx for Lustre file system linked to Amazon S3 can load file contents on first access.
cards.explanation: FSx for Lustre can retrieve a file's contents from its linked S3 repository when first accessed. Preloading needed files avoids that initial retrieval latency.

source.title: Preloading files into your file system

cards.statement: AWS Storage Gateway cached volumes keep their primary data copy on premises.
cards.explanation: Cached volumes keep the primary data in Amazon S3 and retain frequently accessed data locally. The on-premises disks provide a working cache rather than the primary full dataset.
cards.misconception: Cached volumes store the authoritative full dataset locally instead of in Amazon S3.

source.title: How Volume Gateway works

cards.statement: Amazon S3 multipart uploads let an application send different parts of one object in parallel.
cards.explanation: Multipart upload permits concurrent transfers of independent object parts. This lets an application use available bandwidth more effectively for a large upload.

source.title: Uploading and copying objects using multipart upload in Amazon S3

cards.statement: Amazon S3 can return a selected byte range from an object instead of transferring the complete object.
cards.explanation: Byte-range retrieval lets an application fetch the portion of an S3 object it needs. This avoids transferring the remainder when processing part of a large object.

source.title: Performance guidelines for Amazon S3

cards.statement: Amazon EFS Provisioned throughput supports high transfer rates even for file systems storing little data.
cards.explanation: EFS Provisioned throughput is independent of the amount of data stored. A small file system can therefore have throughput provisioned for a demanding workload.

source.title: Amazon EFS performance specifications

cards.statement: Amazon S3 object overwrites use eventual consistency for subsequent reads of the current object.
cards.explanation: S3 provides strong read-after-write consistency for successful object overwrites. A subsequent read reflects a completed overwrite rather than an older value awaiting propagation.
cards.misconception: Overwriting an existing S3 object leaves a period of eventual consistency for subsequent reads.

source.title: What is Amazon S3?

cards.statement: Increasing an AWS Lambda function's memory allocation also increases its available CPU power.
cards.explanation: Lambda allocates CPU power in proportion to configured memory. A CPU-bound function can benefit from a memory increase even when its RAM usage is modest.

source.title: Configure Lambda function memory

cards.statement: AWS Lambda reserved concurrency can reduce cold-start latency by pre-initializing execution environments.
cards.explanation: Provisioned concurrency prepares Lambda execution environments ahead of requests. Reserved concurrency reserves and caps concurrency but does not pre-initialize environments.
cards.misconception: Reserving concurrent Lambda executions also keeps execution environments initialized.

source.title: Configuring reserved concurrency for a function

cards.statement: Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling target tracking scales CPU capacity by resizing running instances.
cards.explanation: Target tracking adjusts an Auto Scaling group's instance capacity toward a utilization target. It launches or terminates instances instead of resizing running instances.
cards.misconception: EC2 Auto Scaling target tracking changes individual instance sizes to meet a CPU utilization target.

source.title: Target tracking scaling policies for Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling

cards.statement: Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling can use SQS backlog per instance to scale a queue-processing worker fleet.
cards.explanation: Backlog per instance relates queued work to the workers available to process it. An Auto Scaling policy can use this metric to keep each worker's pending workload near a target.

source.title: Scaling policy based on Amazon SQS

cards.statement: Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling can schedule extra capacity before a recurring daily traffic peak.
cards.explanation: Scheduled scaling adjusts an Auto Scaling group's capacity at specified times. Predictable demand can be met in advance rather than after a utilization alarm.

source.title: Scheduled scaling for Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling

cards.statement: Amazon ECS Service Auto Scaling directly increases the EC2 instance count to provide room for extra tasks.
cards.explanation: ECS Service Auto Scaling changes the desired task count. If container instances lack resources, extra tasks remain pending until host capacity becomes available.
cards.misconception: Scaling an ECS service directly scales its underlying EC2 host fleet.

source.title: Automatically scale your Amazon ECS service

cards.statement: An Amazon EC2 cluster placement group packs instances into one Availability Zone to reduce inter-instance latency.
cards.explanation: Cluster placement keeps EC2 instances close together within an Availability Zone. This favors tightly coupled workloads that depend on fast communication between instances.

source.title: Placement strategies for your placement groups

cards.statement: An AWS Graviton-based EC2 instance can execute x86-64 application binaries natively.
cards.explanation: Graviton uses the Arm architecture. Native machine-code applications and dependencies need Arm-compatible builds rather than their x86-64 binaries.
cards.misconception: An x86-64 binary can run natively on a Graviton processor unchanged.

source.title: Mixing AWS Graviton with x86 CPUs to optimize cost and resiliency using Amazon EKS

cards.statement: An Elastic Fabric Adapter can bypass the operating system for supported inter-instance communication.
cards.explanation: EFA's operating-system bypass reduces communication overhead for compatible HPC and machine learning libraries, helping tightly coupled workloads exchange data efficiently.

source.title: Elastic Fabric Adapter for AI/ML and HPC workloads on Amazon EC2

cards.statement: A VPC-connected AWS Lambda function can reach the IPv4 internet directly from a public subnet.
cards.explanation: Placing a Lambda function in a public subnet does not give it internet access. IPv4 connectivity needs a suitable egress path, such as a private-subnet route through a NAT gateway.
cards.misconception: A Lambda function acquires direct internet connectivity from a public subnet's internet gateway route.

source.title: Enable internet access for VPC-connected Lambda functions

cards.statement: An Amazon EC2 T3 instance in Standard mode sustains full CPU performance after its CPU credits run out.
cards.explanation: A T3 instance in Standard mode gradually returns to baseline CPU utilization when its accrued credits run out. Sustained bursting requires additional credits.
cards.misconception: Standard-mode T3 instances retain burst-level CPU performance after exhausting their credits.

source.title: Key concepts for burstable performance instances

cards.statement: An AWS Batch array job can run the same containerized workload against many independent input items.
cards.explanation: An array job creates related child jobs from a shared job definition. Each child can process a different input, allowing one submission to coordinate a parallel workload.

source.title: Array jobs

cards.statement: An Amazon RDS read replica can return older data than its source because replication is asynchronous.
cards.explanation: RDS copies source changes to a read replica asynchronously. Applications that read a replica need to tolerate replication lag after a write to the source.

source.title: Working with DB instance read replicas

cards.statement: The Amazon Aurora reader endpoint can spread queries from one connection across multiple reader instances.
cards.explanation: Aurora's reader endpoint balances new connections, not individual queries. Queries sent through an established connection remain on the instance serving that connection.
cards.misconception: The Aurora reader endpoint distributes individual queries rather than database connections.

source.title: Reader endpoints for Amazon Aurora

cards.statement: Distributing Amazon DynamoDB requests evenly across many partition key values helps avoid hot partitions.
cards.explanation: A DynamoDB partition has finite throughput. Spreading activity across partition keys reduces concentrated demand that can overload a partition despite spare table-wide capacity.

source.title: Best practices for designing and using partition keys effectively in DynamoDB

cards.statement: An Amazon DynamoDB global secondary index can serve strongly consistent reads.
cards.explanation: DynamoDB global secondary indexes support eventually consistent reads. Their query results can lag behind recent changes to the underlying table.
cards.misconception: Strong read consistency can be requested from a global secondary index.
cards.volatilityNote: Supported consistency models for global secondary indexes could expand.

source.title: DynamoDB read consistency

cards.statement: A direct write to Amazon DynamoDB can leave an item cached in DynamoDB Accelerator stale.
cards.explanation: A write that bypasses DAX does not refresh its item cache. Cached data can remain stale until the entry expires, is evicted, or is updated through DAX.

source.title: DAX and DynamoDB consistency models

cards.statement: A result filter on an Amazon DynamoDB query reduces the read capacity consumed by that query.
cards.explanation: DynamoDB applies query filters after reading the matching items. Discarding items from the response does not reduce the capacity consumed to read them.
cards.misconception: A DynamoDB query is charged read capacity based on the items retained after filtering.

source.title: Filter expressions for the Query operation in DynamoDB

cards.statement: Lazy loading with Amazon ElastiCache adds a database read when the requested item is absent from the cache.
cards.explanation: With lazy loading, an ElastiCache miss sends the application to the database before the result is cached. The first request for uncached data pays this extra retrieval latency.

source.title: Caching strategies for Memcached

cards.statement: Amazon Aurora serverless can scale an existing DB instance while database transactions are in progress.
cards.explanation: Aurora serverless adjusts compute capacity within its configured range during active database work. Scaling does not require waiting for transactions to finish.

source.title: How Aurora serverless works

cards.statement: Amazon RDS storage autoscaling reduces allocated storage after large tables are deleted.
cards.explanation: RDS storage autoscaling increases allocated storage but does not shrink it. Deleting table data can free space within the existing allocation rather than reduce that allocation.
cards.misconception: RDS storage autoscaling reverses earlier storage increases when database usage falls.
cards.volatilityNote: Automatic storage scale-down support could change as RDS storage capabilities evolve.

source.title: Managing capacity automatically with Amazon RDS storage autoscaling

cards.statement: AWS DMS data migration tasks can translate stored procedure code for a different database engine.
cards.explanation: DMS replication tasks move data between databases. Converting database code for a different engine is a separate step handled by DMS Schema Conversion.
cards.misconception: The data migration task also converts database procedural code between engines.

source.title: Components of AWS DMS

cards.statement: Amazon Redshift can skip storage blocks when a query filters on a table's sort key.
cards.explanation: Redshift records minimum and maximum column values for storage blocks. Sorting data lets range filters exclude blocks whose values fall outside the requested range.

source.title: Sort keys

cards.statement: A promoted Amazon RDS read replica continues receiving replication updates from its former source.
cards.explanation: Promoting an RDS read replica stops its replication relationship with the source. The promoted database becomes an independent DB instance.
cards.misconception: Read replica promotion preserves incoming replication from the original source.

source.title: Promoting a read replica to be a standalone DB instance
